headline: High: Rasa can egress to external APIs while the paired content-writing repo offers no isolation, creating leakage and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection is limited by lack of a documented bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing repo with no runnable I/O surfaces, while profile B is a runnable support bot with many external chat/API surfaces. There is no documented shared channel or default ingestion path between them, so only an unusual manual bridge would let A’s text steer B. That makes injection plausible but limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A-generated text into B’s training, prompts, or message templates, injection becomes possible.
IF B is configured to ingest files or messages produced by A without sanitization, attacker-controlled instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of unreviewed A outputs into B prompt templates.
Add a fixed instruction prefix/suffix around any imported text.
Review B message handlers for prompt-like parsing.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and exposes no I/O surfaces; B touches text/voice and can send traffic through allowlisted network egress and chat APIs. The pair lacks a documented shared filesystem or OAuth principal, so leakage is not default. If operators bridge A’s outputs into B, B can transmit that content externally.
conditions: IF A outputs are pasted into B conversations or configs, those contents may leave the local environment via B’s APIs.
IF both agents are placed in the same shared workspace, accidental disclosure becomes possible.
mitigations: Store A and B in separate directories.
Avoid placing secrets in any text passed from A to B.
Restrict B API connectors to approved channels only.
Turn on manual review for outbound B messages.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write, network, or concurrency capabilities; B has allowlisted egress and does not support multiple instances. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable-resource writes, git state, or shared locks. The main conflict risk is limited to operator-managed shared resources, not a default capability clash.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external resource, conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator multiplexes B instances despite its single-instance model, state contention may appear.
mitigations: Do not grant shared write access to the same resource.
Run only one B instance at a time.
Use separate API credentials per agent.
Check for accidental shared config files.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable store.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing source that can generate persuasive but unverified text; B is a customer-support bot that can act on dialogue and send messages through external channels. Even without a documented direct bridge, if B consumes A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into user-facing responses. The interaction is inferred, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text as a source for replies or actions without verification, incorrect content can be propagated.
IF A produces fabricated facts or citations that B forwards to users, downstream error multiplies.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them.
Add a verification step in B for factual claims.
Limit B to templated responses for high-risk intents.
Log source provenance for any imported text.
requires-engineering: implement citation/fact checking before send.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source content-writing repo with no declared data classes or residency constraints; B is an open-source support bot handling text/voice and external messaging APIs. No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to generic deployment choices rather than the pair itself.
conditions: IF operators route regulated data through B’s external channels, compliance obligations may apply.
IF A is repurposed to store regulated content, its lack of documented controls becomes relevant.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through B.
Document retention settings for B connectors.
Keep A as a reference repo only.
Review deployment region for B integrations.
requires-engineering: add policy controls for regulated data flows.
